itsm._resultIsErrorWhen_note: This server catches its own failures and returns them as SUCCESSFUL tool results - isError is false and the message arrives as ordinary text, e.g. {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Error: Either email or requester_id must be provided"}],"isError":false}. Without this pattern executor.js believes it, so a human can approve a tier_3, get HTTP 200, and have nothing happen - observed doing exactly that on 2026-08-04. The regex is applied ONLY when the entire result is a bare string (see resultIsDeclaredError in executor.js), never to structured output, because a false positive is worse than the bug: it would report a completed action as failed and leave it in the approval queue for a retry that executes it twice. Remove this if upstream starts setting isError properly.
itsm._pin: TWO upstream problems, one pin. (1) freshservice-mcp 1.0.0 declares 'mcp[cli]>=1.3.0' with no upper bound, so uvx resolves mcp 2.0.0, which removed mcp.server.fastmcp - the server dies at import and mcpBackends.js reports a generic 'Connection closed'. Anything below 2 fixes that. (2) Below 2 is not enough: several of its tools are annotated as returning str but return a dict, and from ~1.9 the SDK derives an outputSchema from that annotation and validates against it, so get_ticket_by_id, get_list_of_solution_article and get_solution_article ALL failed with 'validation error ... Output'. Verified 2026-08-04 by flipping the pin on the running pod: under mcp<2 three of six mapped verbs were unusable, under mcp<1.9 all six work. Below 1.9 no outputSchema is emitted at all, so there is nothing to validate. The cost is no structuredContent on any result - tool output reaches the agents as text, which is what the bridge does with it anyway. Revisit if upstream fixes its return annotations, and note this re-resolves on every pod start, so a newly-cut major of any other unbounded dependency can break it again with no change on our side.
itsm._note: Self-hosted community server (github.com/effytech/freshservice_mcp, MIT), run via uvx - stdio transport, not a hosted remote endpoint. Freshworks does have its own native MCP integration, but as of writing it's Beta/EAP-gated to selected Enterprise-plan customers (see developers.freshworks.com/docs/agentic-dev-tools/mcp-server/) - this community server works today without needing that program. FRESHSERVICE_APIKEY comes from Profile Settings -> API Settings in the Freshservice admin panel.
itsm._verified: 2026-08-04: all 6 mapped verbs checked against a live tools/list from freshservice-mcp 1.0.0 (59 tools, confirmed identical from the deployed pod) - filter_tickets, get_ticket_by_id, get_list_of_solution_article, get_solution_article, create_ticket_note and create_ticket all exist. Re-run scripts/list-provider-tools.py freshservice after any version bump; it diffs the mapping against the running server and exits non-zero on a miss.
itsm._write_surface: Those 59 tools include ~20 that write or destroy - delete_ticket, update_ticket, create_service_request, create_agent, create_requester, and the whole solution-article set. Exactly 2 are mapped (create_ticket at tier_3, create_ticket_note at tier_2). The rest have no action-mapping entry and therefore cannot execute at all, which is the intended fail-closed state, NOT an oversight to be tidied up by adding mappings. Note delete_ticket in particular appears in no tier of policy/risk-tiers.yaml either, so it would also fall to default_policy.unlisted_action.
